subject: Redwood adapter: safety & graceful degrade proposal for MidForge integration
messages:
From: Alicia Park <alicia@midforge.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood adapter: safety & graceful degrade proposal for MidForge integration

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the intro with Sergio last week — excited to explore a lightweight adapter to connect MidForge's orchestration layer into Redwood's inference runtime. Attached is a short proposal (PDF) that covers our planned adapter responsibilities, failure modes we want to guard against, and a suggested graceful-degrade strategy if model variants or capacity fall back.

High-level ask: can Redwood engineering validate the safety constraints (auth & data flow), confirm whether automatic fallback to a quantized model is feasible, and note any incompatibilities with Redwood's KV prefix caching approach?

Quick summary of what we included:
- Auth: service-to-service with mTLS + optional per-tenant API key
- Data flow: request metadata stripped on ingress; user content flows to your hosted model for hosted customers, to private endpoints for on-prem customers
- Fallback policy: when primary model latency > 300ms for 95th pct, route to a "low-cost" quantized variant and attach a "degraded: true" response header
- Observability: require request-id propagation and per-request token-level cost logging

Attachments: midforge-redwood-adapter-v1.pdf, midforge-arch-diagram.png

Would appreciate a short read and a go/no-go on the safety and fallback approach. If helpful, Ben (our infra lead) and I can join an engineering call this week.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Park
Head of Partnerships, MidForge Systems

MidForge Systems | midforge.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood adapter: safety & graceful degrade proposal for MidForge integration

Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and the doc, skimmed it and looks sensible. Looping in Sergio (partner tech lead) and Karthik (runtime) to validate a couple of areas quickly.

Initial takeaways and open questions for validation call:
1) Auth & tenancy: mTLS + per-tenant key model works for Hosted + Dedicated. For Private we need to confirm whether customers will allow an inbound connection from MidForge or if the adapter must be deployed in the customer's VPC. Can you confirm your preferred deployment pattern?

2) Fallback path: automatic routing to a quantized variant is doable but we need to confirm two things:
  - Is your quantized variant functionally equivalent (same vocab/tokenization)?
  - Do you have an SLO where partial output (truncated or fewer beams) is acceptable?

3) Caching implications: Redwood's prefix/KV cache expects deterministic prompt preprocessing. If MidForge performs prompt re-writing (e.g., enrichment, redaction) at the adapter layer, we need to capture the pre- and post-hashes so cache-hit metrics remain accurate. Would you be able to produce a short test harness (1000 requests) showing rewrite rate?

4) Observability: we can surface request-id and cost breakdowns, but any PII-sanitization must happen before logs leave the VPC for Private deployments.

Can we schedule a 45-minute technical sync? I have availability: Wed 2025-05-07 10:00-11:00 PT or 15:00-16:00 PT. Please propose one and share any network/firewall constraints.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Integrations | Redwood Inference

> Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and the doc, skimmed it and looks sensible. Looping in Sergio (partner tech lead) and Karthik (runtime) to validate a couple of areas quickly.
> 
> Initial takeaways and open questions for validation call:

Hi Hannah — thanks for the quick review and the good list. Wed 10:00 PT works for us.

Answers in short:
- Deployment: MidForge prefers the adapter run in the customer's VPC when the customer requests Private deployment. For Hosted/Dedicated customers we'll run a managed adapter in our infra that uses mTLS to Redwood endpoints.
- Quantized variant: yes, same tokenizer/vocab. We accept reduced beam count and sometimes shorter max-length as an expected degradation. We'll mark outputs with metadata: {"midforge_degraded": true} when we use that path.
- Prompt rewrite: we do light enrichment (add system tags, remove known PII patterns). We'll provide a 1k-request harness by EOD Tue for you to run against a staging route.

Drive folder with diagrams + harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMidForge-Redwood-Design

We'll join Wed 2025-05-07 10:00 PT. Ben will be on the call to answer infra questions.

Best,
Alicia
